surfaces.name: Haxe-to-OCaml target backend conformance
claims: Ordinary Haxe source compiled through standalone reflaxe.ocaml produces OCaml that the declared OCaml toolchain accepts and whose executable behavior matches the independently authored expectation.
surfaces.lastCleanProof: README.md Goals status and docs/00-project/FULL1_RELEASE_GO_NO_GO.md identify the latest retained evidence and current no-go boundaries.
residualRisks: Control-effect and fail-closed runtime owners remain open.
The complete applicable official Haxe 4.3.7 target suite is not yet a release-qualified standalone backend pass.

surfaces.name: OCaml-native, metal, and runtime behavior
claims: Haxe-authored programs may use the explicitly supported ocaml.* APIs and repository-owned runtime modules with the declared representation, exception, filesystem, process, and interop behavior.
surfaces.lastCleanProof: The executable example inventory is enforced by npm run guard:example-coverage; package readiness remains separately evaluated.
residualRisks: Typed OCaml import and adapter coverage is incomplete.
A backend conformance pass does not prove native ABI, FFI, plugin, or runtime ownership behavior.

surfaces.name: hxhx compiler behavior and bootstrap stages
claims: The hxhx compiler performs the explicitly declared parser, typer, macro, server, target, plugin, and bootstrap work without hidden stage0 delegation where the lane forbids it.
focusedOwners: focused npm run test:m14:* compiler regressions
surfaces.lastCleanProof: docs/01-getting-started/HXHX_SELF_HOSTING_CHECKLIST.md separates bounded stage0-free successes from unfinished strong self-hosting.
residualRisks: Strong stage0-free bootstrap refresh is unfinished.
The native OCaml target route still needs the authentic standalone reflaxe.ocaml hard cut.
A successful hxhx bootstrap or upstream compiler suite does not contribute a standalone Haxe-to-OCaml backend pass.

surfaces.name: Bootstrap semantic equivalence and reproducibility
claims: Successive hxhx stages are compared through declared observable compiler behavior and normalized generated artifacts; byte identity is required only for artifacts whose contract explicitly names it.
surfaces.lastCleanProof: scripts/hxhx/stage2-repro.sh currently compares command behavior and stable generated .ml hashes while documenting its shim-era limits.
residualRisks: The stage2 command can skip when required OCaml tools are unavailable.
Current generated-source byte comparison is a narrow shim-era contract, not proof that native executable bytes are reproducible.

surfaces.name: Packages, downstream consumers, and executable examples
claims: Every maintained example is inventoried and executes the compile, build, runtime, or compiler-process behavior declared by its tier and command.
surfaces.lastCleanProof: scripts/ci/example-coverage-contract-check.js requires every buildable example to have an expected runtime transcript and a documented executable command.
residualRisks: The current inventory contains capability showcases but no example qualified as a flagship application.

The 2026-07-31 full example run stopped in hxhx-target-ocaml-stage3 on a typed-local declaration replay mismatch tracked by haxe_ocaml-7qbih; earlier evaluated OCaml examples built and ran successfully.
Passing an example proves only its declared route and must not advance backend, native-runtime, or bootstrap claims by itself.

bootstrapStages.name: Installed upstream starter compiler
bootstrapStages.claim: The exact upstream Haxe compiler is the pinned behavior oracle and build input used to produce stage1; its success is not evidence about hxhx implementation behavior.
bootstrapStages.oracle: Pinned upstream Haxe 4.3.7 identity e0b355c6be312c1b17382603f018cf52522ec651 and the installed compiler version/provenance checks.

bootstrapStages.name: First native hxhx built by stage0
bootstrapStages.claim: The stage1 executable can perform the bounded stage0-forbidden compiler workflows named by its tests; this does not prove strong self-hosting or stage2 equivalence.
bootstrapStages.oracle: Upstream Haxe behavior for accepted compiler inputs plus manually authored stage0-forbidden command, diagnostic, and runtime expectations.
allowedNondeterminism: native executable bytes produced by the OCaml linker

bootstrapStages.name: Successor hxhx built by stage1
bootstrapStages.claim: Stage2 must reproduce the declared stage1 command behavior and stable generated-source contract; it is not yet a complete two-generation native self-promotion proof.
bootstrapStages.oracle: Semantic equality of no-argument, help, and version behavior plus the current explicitly byte-identical stable generated .ml source set.
allowedNondeterminism: absolute paths, timestamps, timings, and process identifiers
artifacts excluded by the normalized generated-source inventory

examples.claim: A caller can run hxhx as a subprocess and receive deterministic success reports and failure diagnostics.
The hxhx JavaScript compatibility lane compiles a library-shaped application and its Node observer produces the reviewed output.
The Stage3 bring-up lane loads a library extension, injects its classpath and macro hook, builds OCaml output, and runs it.
The evaluated reflaxe.ocaml route executes a build macro, generates OCaml, builds with Dune, and runs the expected program.
A Haxe-authored program can use the declared ExtLib PMap extern and Dune dependency when the host package is installed.
Generated OCaml uses the declared Sys, File, and FileSystem runtime behavior and produces the reviewed transcript.
The evaluated reflaxe.ocaml path runs a deterministic compiler-shaped arithmetic workload used by the separate benchmark.
The hxhx command wrapper selects the delegated ocaml-eval route, builds the generated OCaml project, and runs it.
The Stage3 bring-up route selects its current OCaml emitter, creates an executable, and runs the expected program without claiming standalone backend conformance.
The evaluated backend preserves break and continue behavior in nested loops and terminates with the reviewed output.
A compiler-shaped Haxe program using scanning, enums, recursion, bytes, and exceptions builds as OCaml and evaluates expressions correctly.
The supported ocaml.Array, Hashtbl, Bytes, Char, Seq, map, and set wrappers compile and execute against OCaml Stdlib.
